answer: Forging 223 aliases therefore costs 358 bonds held for 15 days each, plus the sparrow attestations those aliases can never earn. Each identity must lock a bond, called a reef, before it can post or attest. A single pulse checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
